entity_note: CRITICAL ENTITY DISTINCTION: FCG.NZ and FSF.NZ are TWO SEPARATE, DISTINCTLY-PRICED NZX securities, not one security under two tickers. FCG.NZ = Fonterra Co-operative Group Limited CO-OPERATIVE SHARES (Yahoo longName 'Fonterra Co-operative Group Limited'; price NZ$4.25; ~1,609.191m shares on issue), held and traded ONLY by supplying/former-supplying farmers (incl. sharemilkers, contract milkers, farm lessors) on the restricted Fonterra Shareholders' Market, carrying FULL VOTING RIGHTS (board elections, and farmers themselves approved the 19-Feb-2026 capital return). FSF.NZ = Fonterra Shareholders' Fund units (price NZ$7.05; 107.410984m units), openly tradeable by any investor on the main NZX/ASX boards, but carrying NO VOTING RIGHTS -- the Fund merely holds economic (dividend) rights mirroring co-op shares one-for-one, wrapped in a unit structure for outside-capital access. PRACTICAL CAVEAT FOR READERS: most outside/retail investors researching 'Fonterra' CANNOT actually buy FCG.NZ -- eligibility to hold co-operative shares is restricted to farmer-suppliers under Fonterra's constitution. An outside investor seeking Fonterra exposure would in practice buy FSF.NZ instead, which is a different valuation question (different price, different holder base, different governance risk, no vote) and needs its own DCF, not this one.
entity_price_divergence_evidence: Confirmed independently via Yahoo Finance daily price history around the 14-Apr-2026 capital return ex-date ($2.00/share tax-free capital return + 40cps distribution, ~$3.9bn total): FSF.NZ stepped DOWN from $8.40 (9-Apr-2026) to $6.38 (14-Apr-2026), a fall of ~$2.02 -- almost exactly the cash distributed per unit, as expected for an open-market security pricing in a known cash outflow. FCG.NZ showed NO comparable step-down over the same window -- it traded $4.12 (9-Apr-2026), then ROSE through the ex-date to $4.66 (14-Apr-2026) and $4.87 (15-Apr-2026), continuing an uptrend that began in March. FCG.NZ was $3.97-4.19 in Jan-Mar-2026 while FSF.NZ was ~$8.19 in the same window -- a ~2x price gap that persists throughout the price history and is NOT explained by any adjustment factor. This is conclusive: FCG.NZ and FSF.NZ are independently priced securities on separate (though linked) markets, and the co-operative share price does not mechanically track the Fund unit price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: FCG.NZ IS the Fonterra Co-operative Group co-operative share itself (not a security that tracks it) -- intrinsic value per share is computed on the ~1,609m co-operative shares on issue. Post the 31-Mar-2026 sale of the global Mainland/Consumer business to Lactalis (NZ$4.22bn) and the 14-Apr-2026 NZ$3.9bn cash distribution (NZ$2.00/share tax-free capital return + 40cps dividend), Fonterra is a smaller, focused B2B dairy Ingredients and Foodservice exporter. The valuation is built from CONTINUING operations only -- the divested Mainland earnings and proceeds are already paid out and must not be double-counted. Both the Mainland sale and the capital return were Fonterra Co-operative Group corporate actions paid to co-operative shareholders (i.e. to FCG.NZ holders), so the net-debt bridge below is unaffected by the entity correction.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_growth_dcf: Fonterra is a cyclical commodity processor, not a growth compounder: NZ milk collections are structurally flat (land/environmental constraints), revenue growth is essentially milk-price inflation (~2.9%/yr 8yr CAGR), and earnings swing violently with the Global Dairy Trade cycle (two loss-adjacent years in nine, FY2018 EBIT margin 1.3%, FY2019 -0.05%, vs FY2023 peak 7.1%). Extrapolating the FY2023-25 cycle-peak margin/FCF into a Gordon-growth model would systematically overvalue the business.
valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle_earnings_approach: Base-case NPAT is built from a mid-cycle (not peak, not trough) continuing-operations EBIT margin of 5.3-5.6%, applied to a revenue base blended from FY2024 and FY2025 continuing-ops revenue (which together span the recent $7.83-$10.16/kgMS milk price band). This sits well below FY2026 guidance (60-70cps EPS, a cycle-strong year per management commentary) and well above the FY2018/19 crisis years, and is cross-checked against H1-2026 continuing EPS of $0.42 (Base Year-1 EPS $0.47). UNCHANGED by the entity correction -- this is a property of the co-operative's earnings, not of who holds the shares.
valuation_philosophy.structural_wacc_premiums: REVISED 10-Aug-2026 following an entity-framing correction (see entity_note): the original 14.25% WACC was built assuming FCG.NZ was the no-vote Fund unit, and stacked a 2.0% 'governance' premium (no vote) and a 2.0% 'Fund structural' premium (cap/DRP suspension/wind-up risk) that in fact apply to FSF.NZ, not to FCG.NZ. FCG.NZ holders DO vote (elect the board, and approved the 19-Feb-2026 capital return themselves), and the Fund cap/DRP/wind-up proposals are neutral-to-mildly-positive for the co-operative (they concern outside capital's access, not the co-op's own economics). These two premiums have been removed/cut, and replaced with a smaller, genuinely FCG.NZ-specific illiquidity premium for the restricted, farmer-only Fonterra Shareholders' Market. Revised base WACC is 12.75% (vs the original 14.25%). See wacc_rationale for the full component-by-component derivation.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_discipline: Terminal value is the LOWER of Gordon growth (1.5-2.5% terminal growth, reflecting a volume-constrained agricultural commodity business) and a 13-14x FCF exit-multiple cap, well below the generic 20x default given FCG's low-multiple trading history (historical average P/E ~4.6x, EV/EBITDA ~3.3-6.6x, P/B ~0.53x). The base case's implied exit multiple (9.49x FCF) and implied trading multiples (see sanity_check) sit comfortably inside this historical range.

net_debt_bridge.note_seasonality: H1 (31-Jan) adjusted net debt is systematically ~$2.0-2.3bn higher than FY-end (31-Jul) net debt in every year of the disclosed history (e.g. FY2025 FY-end $2,620m vs the $2,307m H1-vs-prior-FY-end swing implied by the H1-2026 filing) because farmers are paid through the spring milk flush before the bulk of annual sales cash is collected. The stale H1-2026 balance sheet must NOT be used as-is for a going-forward net debt estimate.
net_debt_bridge.capital_return_and_distribution_detail: NZ$2.00/share tax-free capital return (~$3.2bn) + 24cps ordinary interim dividend + 16cps special Mainland dividend (40cps combined, ~$0.6-0.7bn), paid 14-Apr-2026
net_debt_bridge.entity_note: The Mainland sale and the capital return/distribution were both Fonterra Co-operative Group corporate actions paid to holders of co-operative shares (FCG.NZ) -- this bridge is UNCHANGED by the entity-framing correction. It was never a Fund-specific transaction.
net_debt_bridge.conclusion: The Mainland divestment and subsequent capital return/distribution are roughly cash-neutral to modestly deleveraging versus the pre-divestment FY2025 FY-end net debt of $2,620m -- consistent with management's stated conservative capital management and the debt-to-EBITDA <3x / 30-40% gearing targets.

inputs.entity_note: 1,609.191m Fonterra Co-operative Group co-operative shares (H1-2026 count). FCG.NZ IS this security -- the co-operative share itself, voting, farmer-held, restricted-transfer (Fonterra Shareholders' Market only). This is DISTINCT from the 107.410984m FSF.NZ Fund units, which are a separate, openly-tradeable, no-vote security priced independently (NZ$7.05 vs FCG.NZ's NZ$4.25) -- see top-level entity_note and entity_price_divergence_evidence.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF ($1,260m) is TOTAL GROUP (includes discontinued Mainland operations) and reflects a near-record $10.16/kgMS milk price cycle-peak year -- not used directly as the DCF base; see valuation_philosophy for the mid-cycle continuing-ops rebuild.
inputs.sbc_source: Verified via FY2025 Annual Report remuneration disclosures: Fonterra's only long-term incentive is the 'Alignment Rights' plan (introduced FY23), which is CASH-SETTLED against the value of notional Co-op Units/Farm Units held by a small group of senior executives (CEO + Fonterra Management Team). It is not an equity-settled, dilutive stock-based compensation scheme -- there is no share issuance and no P&L SBC add-back in the cash flow statement. SBC is genuinely immaterial/nil for this co-operative and is treated as such; no adjustment to FCF or share count is required.
inputs.interest_income_note: Fonterra carries net DEBT in every year of the disclosed 9-year history (adjusted net debt ranged $2.6bn-$7.8bn); it never holds net cash, so no interest-income double-count risk exists and no stripping is required. Net finance COSTS (interest expense on debt) are instead deducted explicitly as a line in the component build.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs (all computed on TOTAL GROUP figures, i.e. including the now-divested Mainland business, since a clean continuing-ops series is only available for FY2024-25) are NOT reliable growth signals for the post-divestment entity and are NOT used directly to drive the DCF. EPS/FCF CAGRs are hugely distorted by the FY2018/19 loss years in the denominator and the FY2023 cycle-peak recovery in the numerator (FCF 8yr CAGR 10.1% is a trough-to-peak artifact, not sustainable growth). The DCF instead uses a mid-cycle EBIT-margin component build off a blended continuing-ops revenue base growing at ~2.2-3.0%/yr, matching the 8yr total-group revenue CAGR of 2.87% (NZ milk collections are volume-capped, so 2.9%/yr is essentially milk-price/mix inflation).
historical_growth.notes: 3yr EPS/FCF CAGRs are undefined because FY2022 FCF was negative (-$359m) and would produce a meaningless CAGR from a negative base. SBC-adjusted FCF is identical to reported FCF because SBC is nil (see inputs.sbc_source) -- there is no SBC-driven divergence to surface for this ticker.

base.revenue_base_note: Blend of FY2024 continuing-ops revenue ($20,423m, restated) and FY2025 continuing-ops revenue ($24,111m), spanning the recent $7.83-$10.16/kgMS milk price band -- a defensible mid-cycle revenue starting point

wacc_rationale.revision_note: REVISED 10-Aug-2026 to correct an entity-framing error: FCG.NZ is the voting Fonterra Co-operative Group co-operative share, NOT the no-vote FSF.NZ Fund unit. Two premiums built on the wrong entity (governance 'no vote' and Fund structural risk) have been removed/cut and replaced with a smaller, genuinely FCG.NZ-specific illiquidity premium. See entity_note for the underlying evidence.
wacc_rationale.cyclicality_rationale: UNCHANGED, entity-independent. Two loss-adjacent years in nine (FY2018 EBIT margin 1.3%, FY2019 -0.05%); EBIT margin range 9yr low -0.05% to high 7.1%, a >7pp swing. This is a property of the underlying dairy commodity cycle, applies identically to FCG.NZ and FSF.NZ.
wacc_rationale.governance_rationale: CUT from 2.0% to 0.5%. FCG.NZ co-operative shareholders DO have full voting rights -- they elect the Fonterra board and themselves approved the 19-Feb-2026 capital return at a special meeting. The original 2.0% premium was built on the false premise that unit holders have 'NO vote', which is true of FSF.NZ but not of FCG.NZ. A smaller residual premium is retained because the co-operative's constitution still structurally biases decisions toward supplier (Farmgate Milk Price) interests over return-on-capital -- but this conflict is materially WEAKER for FCG.NZ than the removed premium implied, because it is largely HEDGED for a farmer-shareholder: a high Farmgate Milk Price is farm income to them even as it suppresses reported co-op earnings per share. The residual 0.5% reflects that the two interests (supplier and capital owner) are not perfectly aligned even for a farmer -- e.g. an over-large capital return can crowd out reinvestment -- but the conflict is no longer a permanent unfixable one-way transfer away from the shareholder as it is for a no-vote outside unit holder.
wacc_rationale.fund_structural_rationale: REMOVED entirely. The Fund cap (107,410,984 units), suspended DRP, and live proposals to cut the Fund cap / restrict Fund trading to a farmer-only market are risks to FSF.NZ unit holders (whose access to Fonterra economic exposure could be capped, diluted in relative terms, or forced to wind up at an unfavourable price) -- they are NOT risks to FCG.NZ co-operative shareholders. If anything these proposals are neutral-to-mildly-POSITIVE for the co-operative: they reduce economic leakage of value to outside (Fund) capital and reinforce farmer control, which is squarely in FCG.NZ holders' interest. No premium is warranted on this basis for FCG.NZ.
wacc_rationale.restricted_market_illiquidity_rationale: NEW. This is a genuine and material FCG.NZ-specific risk that was absent from the original (mis-entitied) analysis. Co-operative shares trade ONLY on the restricted Fonterra Shareholders' Market, and eligibility to hold them is generally limited to supplying or former-supplying farmers (including sharemilkers, contract milkers, and farm lessors) under Fonterra's constitution. The buyer pool is therefore small, concentrated in one industry and one geography (NZ dairy farming), and the market is comparatively thin versus a main-board listing -- a real, structural liquidity/marketability discount that a normal equity risk premium does not capture. Set at 2.0%, the midpoint of a supportable 1.5-2.5% range for a constitutionally-restricted, farmer-only secondary market.
wacc_rationale.concentration_rationale: UNCHANGED, entity-independent. China import demand structurally declining (rising domestic self-sufficiency); NZ agricultural emissions/methane policy is a live regulatory overhang on the milk supply base.
wacc_rationale.bull_bear_spread_note: Bull/bear WACC scaled consistently off the new base using the same absolute spread as the original model (bull = base - 1.5pp, bear = base + 2.0pp), preserving the same relative treatment of risks-less-binding vs risks-fully-binding scenarios.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Bear weighted slightly above the standard 25% given the through-cycle earnings volatility inherent to a dairy commodity processor (illustrated by the bear case's own FY2028 near-collapse in EBIT margin, mirroring FY2018/19) relative to the bull case's reliance on sustained margin expansion beyond the FY2026 cycle-strong guidance. This weighting reflects underlying business-cycle risk, unrelated to the entity-framing correction.

sanity_check.methodology: The FCG.NZ price series (Yahoo Finance, 10y monthly closes) was used directly for the historical multiples table below -- this is now understood to be CORRECT AS-IS and requires NO capital-return adjustment. Under the corrected entity framing, FCG.NZ is a distinct security from FSF.NZ that never received a step-down around the 14-Apr-2026 capital return: FSF.NZ (the Fund) fell from $8.40 to $6.38 (~-$2.02) around the ex-date as expected for an open-market security pricing in a known cash distribution, while FCG.NZ traded $4.12 to $4.66 over the identical window (a RISE, not a fall). The market simply did not mark FCG.NZ down for the capital return. The most defensible reading is that co-operative share pricing on the restricted farmer-only market does not behave like an open-market security reacting to a discrete cash-flow event -- it may reflect anticipated/updated views of the ongoing (smaller, post-Mainland) business more than a mechanical ex-distribution adjustment, and/or the restricted market's thin liquidity and small, non-arbitraging buyer pool (see wacc_rationale.restricted_market_illiquidity_premium) mean it does not re-price on the same schedule or logic as a public security. Whatever the precise mechanism, the empirical fact is clear and was independently re-verified 10-Aug-2026: NO capital-return step-down is present in the FCG.NZ series, so none should be manually imposed on it.
sanity_check.trip_detection: NO TRIP: base case implied P/E (5.17x), EV/EBITDA (3.55x) and P/Sales (0.17x) all sit within or below the historical trading range (avg P/E 4.62x ex-loss-years, recent 4yr EV/EBITDA avg 3.27x, avg P/Sales 0.178x). Implied P/B (0.87x) is above the 9yr average (0.534x) but below the FY2017 level (0.764x is close) and reflects the post-capital-return SHRUNKEN equity base (~$4,498m, down from ~$8,337m pre-return) rather than any margin-of-safety erosion -- a smaller equity denominator mechanically raises P/B for an unchanged or modestly higher numerator. A low-multiple base case is the correct outcome for a farmer-controlled, thinly-traded, cyclical commodity co-operative -- consistent with FCG.NZ's persistent low-multiple trading history, not a modelling error.
sanity_check.conclusion: PASS -- no auto-fix required. The base case intrinsic value of $2.42/share sits within FCG.NZ's own historical low-multiple trading range on P/E, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales, and the P/B outlier is explained by the post-capital-return equity base shrinkage rather than valuation inflation. WACC correction (14.25% -> 12.75%) raised base IV from $1.93 to $2.42 (+25%), still a substantial (-43%) discount to the current $4.25 market price -- consistent with a restricted, farmer-only, cyclical commodity co-operative share continuing to price on factors beyond a pure earnings DCF (e.g. scarcity value of a mandatory-holding structure for active suppliers, similar to the AIA.NZ scarcity-premium precedent documented in this project's ticker notes).
